name: Terra-Antiqua
description: Terra-Antiqua is an old world, its geological features worn smooth by billions of years of wind and water until even the mountain ranges have been reduced to gentle, rolling uplands that barely qualify for the name. The true drama lies in the canyons, vast gorges carved by patient rivers that expose sedimentary layers stretching back to the planet's formation, each stratum a chapter in a history book written in stone. Petrified forests in the lowland basins preserve the remains of flora that once towered even higher than the current giants.

The atmosphere is rich and clean, carrying the scent of the immense forests that cover the temperate zones in unbroken canopy. The trees of Terra-Antiqua are the planet's defining feature: species that reach heights exceeding two hundred meters, their trunks wide enough to carve dwellings from, their canopies forming a secondary landscape far above the forest floor where entire ecosystems exist without ever touching the ground. Light at ground level is perpetual twilight, filtered through layer after layer of leaves.

The fossilized megafauna in the canyon walls tell of an era when enormous creatures roamed the surface, some rivaling the largest dinosaurs of Earth in scale. What killed them remains debated: the fossil record shows a relatively sudden disappearance approximately fifty million years ago, after which the flora expanded to fill every available niche. Some theories suggest the megafauna were outcompeted by the very plants that now dominate, a slow-motion botanical conquest that replaced animal complexity with vegetative persistence.

Terra-Antiqua has been proposed as a colonization candidate due to its breathable atmosphere and fertile soils, but the dense forests present practical challenges for settlement. Clearing land provokes rapid regrowth that can overwhelm structures within years, and the root networks of the giant trees extend deep enough to undermine foundations laid in what appears to be open ground. The world seems to want to remain forested, and human presence may ultimately require adaptation to the trees rather than removal of them. Timber harvesting is profitable but must be carefully managed to prevent the forest from simply reclaiming everything taken.
